sources.entry: What's Up Docker | Get notified when new versions of your container images are released

summary.one_liner: What's Up Docker (WUD) is a self-hosted tool that watches running containers across Docker, Swarm, Kubernetes, Compose and Nomad, detects newer image versions in registries, and sends notifications or triggers automatic updates.
summary.what_it_does: WUD scans container environments for running workloads and compares their current image tags and digests against what is available in container registries. It supports semantic version analysis and tag filtering via include/exclude rules, regular expressions, transforms, and version pinning. When an update is found, it can send alerts through many channels (e.g. Discord, Slack, Telegram, Ntfy, SMTP, Home Assistant, MQTT) or automatically pull new images and recreate containers for Docker, Docker Compose, or Nomad. It also offers a web dashboard, a REST API, a Prometheus /metrics endpoint, role-based access control with OIDC single sign-on, and a headless one-shot CLI mode for CI/CD pipelines and cron jobs that can fail a build when updates are available. Per-container configuration is done with Docker labels or Kubernetes annotations.
use_cases: get notified when Docker container images have new versions
automatically update running Docker or Compose containers
monitor Kubernetes deployments for newer image tags
check for image updates in CI/CD pipelines before deploying
watch private registry images such as GHCR, ECR or Harbor
send container update alerts to chat or push notification apps
how_to_run: Or use Docker Compose with the getwud/wud:latest image, ports 3000:3000, and the Docker socket mounted
Open the web UI on port 3000 and log in with the admin credentials
One-shot CLI: docker run --rm -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock -e WUD_RUN_MODE=oneshot getwud/wud:latest watch
notable: Watches Docker, Swarm, Kubernetes, Compose and Nomad workloads from one tool
30+ notification and auto-update triggers, including MQTT with Home Assistant auto-discovery
One-shot headless CLI mode with NDJSON output and a --fail-on-update flag for CI gating
Registry webhooks trigger immediate checks, including GitLab Self-Managed
Role-based access control (admin, rw, ro) with personal API tokens and OIDC login
caveats: Automatic updates are only listed for Docker, Docker Compose and Nomad
Docker watching needs the Docker socket mounted or a remote TLS engine configured
Several registries and triggers need their own credentials or setup, described in the external documentation
